_comment: Running list of player-facing patch notes for the NEXT release. As work ships, append entries here. The patch-notes skill rolls this into Assets/data/patchnotes.json on release and clears pending. Categories: feature, balance, fix, polish, content.

entries.line: PawPad chat, effects and alerts lists now show a slim scrollbar so you can see where you are.
Trade Board: offers are now a 3-column card grid with ALL / I CAN FILL / I NEED / MINE filters (R cycles), and the keyboard walks the grid.
Online hub: tamer heads are round everywhere, POST OFFER is a normal button, the trade and guild cards are rebalanced, and the keyboard now reaches JOIN VOICE.

Online hub: battle tiles now have real Find a Match / Play Ranked / Battle the AI buttons, bigger text, location art fading into each tile, and beasts that never cover the labels; leaderboards and Online Now show Steam avatars.
Guild data now loads correctly on startup - weekly goals and member info were silently failing to fetch every boot.
PawPad chat: the SEND button now works with the mouse (taps were landing on the text box instead). Enter still sends too.

Beastbook: the beast art viewer (click a portrait to zoom) now matches the Specimen Hall look — the beast stands on the hall's specimen disc with a placard-style header, replacing the old off-theme purple backdrop. The viewer also animates open and closed, and its buttons now react to hover.

Beastbook: the specimen dial now slowly rotates around your beast — on the main stage and in the art viewer — like a live field scanner (the scale ruler stays put). The big registry number moved to a clean corner stamp instead of hiding behind the beast's head.

Five new beasts join the Beastbook (#16–20): Gnoll → Gnollium (a forest gnome line drawn from European hidden-folk myth), Jackacabra (a chupacabra-hare shadow predator that slips into Weaverton's pastures at dusk to raid the Sheepot flocks), and Padlip → Liliprince (a frog-prince line based on the Brothers Grimm tale — Water until the curse breaks, then Water/Spirit). All five by Jet.

Region identity pass — the three launch zones now share a single story. Saltmoor Cove → Weaverton, the wool-and-loom village built around the Sheepot trade. The Witherwood → Weaverwood, the dye-leaf forest east of town where the herders take their flocks each summer. Old Saltmoor → Weavermere, the mirror-still pond above Weaverton where the village's painters and dye-masters chase the colors no loom can match.

AI-generated wild beasts retired pre-launch — the Beastbook is now a tighter, all-handmade roster. The starter pool, the Weaverwood, and the Weavermere now spawn only handmade species (the old AI-gen beasts still exist in the species DB so prior contracts don't break, just hidden from the book).

Weaverwood (Lv 10) is now the Gnoll/Jackacabra hunting ground — Gnoll spawns wild, Jackacabra prowls the wood's edge raiding Sheepot flocks, and Wishlift + Twincoil drift in from the village pasture. Gnollium is evo-only or boss-roll; Liliprince is boss-only at Weavermere.

Side quests + trade nodes retuned around the new handmade roster — the Weaverwood now offers a Jackacabra cull bounty, a Gnollcap tribute, a Twincoil weave, and the Weavermere's three artist NPCs (Painter Selene, Dye-Master Wren, the Wandering Poet) trade Padlip pondlight motes for relics, dye recipes, and verses.

Beastbook grid no longer stretches non-square monster art — Seraphiel and Aurael, whose source canvases are wider than they are tall, are now rendered at proper proportion instead of being squashed/stretched into a 180x180 box. Aurael in particular shows much more wing/halo/blade detail.

Day 7 streak reward swapped from a Legendary beast to a Master Ink — guaranteed contract on your next attempt. The legendary tier isn't live in open beta yet, so the old reward couldn't actually be granted in any meaningful form.

Beastbook #1–19 balance pass — growth rates raised across the launch roster so beasts level up faster, BSTs reined in to fit their rarity bands (Gnoll/Gnollium/Padlip trimmed, Liliprince pushed up to Rare-tier parity), Jackacabra contract rate eased to 0.35. Jackacabra now learns a signature move Goatsucker's Drain (Lv 38) — heals for 50% of damage dealt — and Liliprince learns a signature Sovereign's Boon (Lv 55) — 90-power Spirit special that heals the caster 25%.

Five new flavor signature moves for Beastbook #10–14: Sheepot learns Pot Guard (Lv 21, raises DEF + SpD), Cerametz learns Solstice Veil (Lv 38, heals 33% wrapped in solstice fleece), Wishlift learns Dream Drift (Lv 19, drifts a spent-wish bubble across the foe's eyes for sleep), Twincoil learns Two-Faced Strike (Lv 19, the outer head bites + the inner head hexes, guaranteed -1 ATK), and Heartwell learns Inner Stillness (Lv 21, the sokushinbutsu monk's meditation — heals 33% and cleanses status). Gothsire's late movelist also retuned: whirlpool_surge moved to Lv 40 as a proper Water capstone, current_boost slid down to Lv 26 where it actually gets used.

Embark popup completely redesigned in the Persona-stamp battle-UI dialect — team slots now show big sprite art carved into a diagonal slab on the left, italic-skewed display name on the right, gold Lv pill, gold-edged element badges, and a prominent HP bar. Reads as a sibling of the battle nameplates instead of a generic list row.

Embark popup roster now actually fits 5+ beasts per row at full card size — was previously clipping the 5th card on a row of 4 due to a stack of three engine quirks (a transformed ancestor, a ghost hover-scale on the cards, and a stale `overflow: hidden` on the world map container) that all conspired to collapse the available width. Layout's been rebuilt to dodge all three.

Embark popup no longer teleports from the top-left to the center on open. The entrance animation was authored back when the modal centered via a transform offset; switching to flex-centering left the offset stuck on the keyframes, sending the modal to the corner for 0.22s before it snapped back.

Wishlift gains an evolution — Wishstar (#13, Wind/Spirit, Rare). When a Wishlift carries enough wishes home the wishes outweigh her, and what falls out the other side is a king with a planet for a body and a sun for a crown — each continent etched across him is a dream that found its way back. Evolves at Lv 32. Art by Spookior.
Achievement descriptions now use 'Contract' terminology throughout — 'Contract your first monster', 'Contract 100 monsters', etc. — consistent with the rest of the game.
Removed loyalty references from UI to match current design (loyalty system was retired pre-launch).
Fixed Branchling's description, which contained unfilled template placeholders from an earlier data pass.
Achievement panel and Shop now use the Persona-stamp dialect on their hero CTAs (Claim All / Buy buttons) and titles.
Mini-expeditions added — short optional adventures that branch off the main path and offer exclusive rewards. The first one unlocks after clearing Weavermere.
Tuned XP yields across the launch roster — wild encounters now grant XP appropriate to their rarity and evolution stage.
Rarity bands rebalanced — Epic now sits properly above Rare in the stat ladder. A new beast line lands in the new Epic band, waiting somewhere off the path above Weavermere.
New beast line added — descend into a hidden mini-expedition near Weavermere to find them.
Whispering Hollow mini-expedition marker tooltip no longer clips off the left map edge — tooltip now anchors to the right of the pin instead of above it.

Clicking a mini-expedition on the world map now opens a full detail panel (drops, beasts, level, waves, boss) before you embark — same flow as main zones. Loomweaver's detail card shows a 'Cannot Contract' tag since it's evo-only.
Whispering Hollow now hosts a varied wild pool — Threadlet shares the cave with Cerametz, Twincoil, and Wishlift.
Threadlet now appears as a rarer wild encounter in Whispering Hollow.
Removed an empty Adventure Wave radio station entry — expedition music context is reserved and will be filled when tracks are ready.

Battle status indicators redesigned with clearer icons and color coding — Burn, Freeze, Paralyze, Poison, Sleep, and Confuse each have a distinct icon and tinted badge instead of generic emoji glyphs. Breeding panel egg icon updated to match the game's icon style.

Burn and Poison hit harder — Burn now ticks for 1/15 of MaxHP per turn (was 1/20) and Poison ticks for 1/10 (was 1/12). Status conditions are meaningful pressure again, especially in longer boss fights.
Internal save migration cleanup — minor save-load speedup.
Threadlet line text polish — clearer signature move descriptions and a small description tune.
Evolutions now play a proper transformation sound instead of a generic UI click.
Cleaned up unused leaderboard categories that weren't surfacing meaningful data.

Guild officers with pending join requests can now actually see them — the Invite button correctly opens the join requests list when requests are pending, instead of always jumping to the invite-player picker. The Invite Player option is still accessible via a button inside the requests panel.

Pending guild join requests panel refreshed — stamped title, bordered request cards with left accent and stagger entrance animation, ACCEPT/DENY buttons in the Beastborne dialect, and time-since timestamps replacing the stale ranked RP display.

Invite Player picker refreshed — header icon, close button, online indicator dot, level badge for offline friends, and empty-state messaging. Both the picker and the requests panel now share the same card chrome (dark solid border, offset purple drop shadow).
Guild invites can now reach friends you've previously played with — not just tamers in your current lobby. Online friends show a green dot; offline friends show their level.
Dewdrop joins the handmade roster — a small round waterdrop with a single leaf for a cap, now Water/Nature dual-typed. Drifts across Weavermere alongside Padlip and the other pond wilds. Art by Jet.

Main-menu → game transition rebuilt — a Persona-style diagonal wipe: gold and purple slabs sweep in to cover the screen, the mascot and BEASTBORNE wordmark stamp over the seam, then the slabs split open to reveal your Hub. (The old transition stopped animating after the engine update.)

Dewdrop now evolves — Duodew (#24, Water/Nature, Uncommon) at Lv 30. The drop that found water still enough to never leave: it roots into the pond floor, raises a leaf overhead like a parasol, and tends a second little drop at its side — the next Dewdrop, not ready to drift. Learns a signature move, Wellspring Surge (Lv 34): a 90-power Water special that heals it for 25% of the damage dealt. Art by Jet.

Stomplet → Skunkape — a new bigfoot shepherd line walks the Weaverwood. Stomplet is the young leafy giant who tends the Sheepot flocks; Skunkape is the elder, mossy and leaf-crowned. Contract a Stomplet in the forest and evolve it at Lv 32. Art by Jet.

Repaired expedition achievement milestones — 'Clear all expeditions' (Conqueror) now actually unlocks at 3 zones cleared instead of 16, and the Weaverwood and Weavermere step achievements now trigger correctly. Hard Mode equivalents fixed to match.
Skunkape's Beastbook evolution chain now correctly shows Stomplet as its pre-evolution.
Skill tree SP counter now just shows your available skill points instead of a confusing X / total fraction. The number is the SP you have to spend, no hidden cap.

Element colors normalized — Nature is consistently emerald-green, Wind is consistently teal. Pills, gradients, borders, badges, move buttons, and the battle UI now match their element icons across every panel.

Burn, Poison, Paralyze, and Freeze status effects now actually persist turn-over-turn instead of self-clearing after a single tick. The recent status damage buff (Burn 1/15, Poison 1/10) now delivers as designed.
Fixed a buggy evolution-upgrade entry on the Duskstalker line that had Umbral Claw evolving into itself — harmless no-op cleaned up.
Pollen Burst now actually does what its description says — 10% chance to poison the target, in line with other Nature/toxin moves.
Dual-type beasts (Dewdrop, Cerametz, Wishstar, Liliprince, Manehelm, Lochmaw, Twincoil, Loomweaver) now show both element badges in the roster and team-picker card views, not just their primary type.
Loomweaver's Beastbook entry now shows a 'Cannot Contract' badge alongside its rarity — it's evolution-only, so this was previously missing context for players who found it in the book.

Stomplet and Skunkape rebalanced into proper Uncommon and Rare bands. Stomplet picks up Sapling Stomp at Lv 21 (60-power Nature physical that hardens the user's stance). Skunkape gets Shepherd's Vigil at Lv 55 (90-power Nature special that pulls life back into the caster).

Dewdrop's moveset refreshed to match its identity — rebuilt around a leaf-capped waterdrop bobbing on still ponds at dawn. Dropped the off-brand ocean/striking moves (no limbs, no surf), traded for pond-mist Water specials (Tidal Pulse, Waterlog, Monsoon Call, Deep Pressure), dawn-light Spirit moves (Spirit Breeze, Aether Pulse), a dawn-mist Wind shield (Gust Shield Lv 22), and the new signature Leafcap Drift at Lv 28 (50-power Nature special, 30% to put the foe to sleep — the leaf-cap dipping forward and the pondsteam doing the rest).

Roster-wide moveset lore audit — every learnable move now has a clear reason that specific beast would know it. Wishlift sheds claw and tackle moves she doesn't have (she drifts on dream-bubbles, not pounces) and picks up Spirit Breeze + Aether Pulse for the dream-light fae flavor. Heartwell, the sokushinbutsu monk under the village fountain, drops his striking moves for the calm vow they belie — gains Aether Pulse (the patient pulse that always lands) and Deep Pressure (the well's settled weight). Padlip the pondfrog sheds ocean-flavored moves (he lives in lily-pads, not the sea) and picks up Tidal Pulse for the throat-sac vibration plus Aqua Shield for the bubble around his body. Cherune the novice cherub trades a feint-jab for Spirit Breeze — guardians leave warmth, not stings.

Heartwell and Twincoil — both standalone Commons that never evolve — got a stat-band lift toward the middle of their tier. Heartwell (BST 267 → 297) leans deeper into the sokushinbutsu monk's identity with more HP and SpD; the well's weight is harder to disturb now. Twincoil (BST 263 → 290) gains a touch more bite and serpentine quickness across the board. Both feel viable into mid-game instead of falling off the moment the player's starter mid-evolves.

Trait pills now show a unique icon per trait — Kindle Heart gets a campfire, Phantom Step gets footprints, Trickster gets a masquerade mask, Lightning Rod gets an antenna, and so on across the full 38-trait roster.

Strict moveset lore pass across the full launch roster — every learnable move now defends itself against the beast's specific identity. Timid beasts stopped learning Intimidate (Sheepot, Pagefin, Stomplet, Wishlift, Cherune); brooding-loyal beasts stopped 'wrath' and 'annihilate' moves that clashed with their patience (Cerametz, Gnollium, Skunkape, Manehelm sentinel); freshwater pond-monks stopped saltwater 'brine/sea/tidal-ward' moves (Heartwell, Liliprince); a king who sleeps standing stopped learning Agility Boost and Tornado Dive (Wishstar); a TIMID flame-foal stopped war-crying (Embrik). Replacements stay in-pool but lean into each beast's actual description — Sheepot picks up Parasite Spore for its fragile-root underside, Skunkape's elder-shepherd kit gets Bloom Burst / Verdant Edge / Overgrowth Slam instead of generic 'crushing/vicious/annihilate' verbs, Wishstar gains Calm Air to match its standing-sleep, Heartwell picks up Warding Hymn + Spirit Link for the monk's vows, and Cherune gets Luminous Wall + Aether Pulse for the guardian-cherub identity that awakens fully at evolution. Dewdrop's Nature dual-typing gets a light touch — the leaf-cap learns Nature Shield (Lv 20, the leaf curls over the drop) and Blade Leaf (Lv 23, leaf-flick edge) on top of the existing Leafcap Drift signature, while keeping its sturdy pond-water core intact.

Hard Mode unlocked per-expedition — clear an expedition on Normal to unlock its Hard variant. Tougher fights (+25% enemy levels, +15% ATK/SpA, +10% HP/DEF/SpD, speed unchanged), bigger rewards (2× XP, 2× gold, 1.5× drop rate), and a zone-specific Hard Token currency awarded on clear — Tide Tokens from Weaverton, Loom Tokens from Weaverwood, Dawn Tokens from Weavermere, Threaded Tokens from Whispering Hollow. Each zone tracks Hard unlock and first-Hard-clear independently.

Expedition team selection now shows a NORMAL / HARD difficulty toggle before you embark. Hard mode (once unlocked for that zone) turns the BEGIN EXPEDITION button red and shows a small HARD MODE kicker above it.

If the save server is unreachable on a machine with no local backup, you're now shown a clear prompt with Retry and Play Offline options instead of silently starting a fresh save that could overwrite your real cloud save on reconnect.

Help tab refreshed — status effect tick rates and persistence updated (Burn 1/15 MaxHP, Poison 1/10 MaxHP, both persist until healed), Whispering Hollow mini-expedition added to the Zones section, dual-type beast list added to the Elements section, Online Hub section updated to reflect the 3-tab launch layout, and Contract/Beastbook terminology cleaned throughout.
Auto-Battler UI and code removed — the feature was scope-cut and the leftover plumbing was dead weight.

Contract encounter UI polish — the radial panel now shows a gold 'CONTRACT · LV X' kicker above the creature sprite, the diamond frame switches to an element-tinted border instead of a flat background fill, and the approach-match indicator uses a cleaner star icon.

Fusion Complete reveal redesigned — result now appears in a 3-stage cinematic sequence: dark wash → beast portrait slides in with its species name → gene table drops in showing each stat vs both parents (green if better than average, red if worse). Two CTAs replace the old Continue button: 'VIEW BEAST' (gold border, routes to your roster) and 'FUSE AGAIN' (ghost, returns to parent picker).
Tamer Card 'Share in Chat' button now plays a sound and shows a toast confirmation when clicked — previously the card was being posted but there was no feedback so it felt broken.

Tutorial walkthrough refreshed for the current game — contract approach count corrected (four approaches, not twelve), Hard Mode mentioned in the closing step, and winning or losing an expedition now plays a victory or defeat sound instead of silence.

Hit-flash on damage taken — sprites now snap to a single bright-white flash for 80ms when struck, instead of the old 400ms red-flicker that dragged across the camera shake. Fighting-game-tight; hits actually feel like hits now.
KO collapse — when a beast faints it now slumps forward 25° while dropping, instead of just translating straight down. Reads as a knocked-out monster rather than a teleport-out.

Status conditions now show ambient halos on the sprite in battle, not just an icon on the nameplate. Burn flickers orange, Poison pulses purple, Paralyze zaps yellow every couple seconds, Freeze sits in a still cyan wash, Sleep breathes slow blue, and Confuse wobbles pink. You can read what's on a beast from across the screen.
Chat, Radio, Active Effects, and Notifications popups can now be dragged anywhere on screen — grab the header to reposition. Each popup remembers where you moved it between sessions.
Toast notifications no longer reappear after you dismiss them — they stay gone until a new one arrives.
Beast descriptions tightened — every launch beast now reads as a clean 1-2 sentence identity instead of a paragraph.
Trade request popup upgraded — lucide swap icon, gold italic 'TRADE REQUEST' kicker, and canonical Accept/Decline button styles.

Move selection panel refreshed — category icons (Physical/Special/Status) are now lucide icons in a counter-rotated diamond badge; PWR, PP, and ACC shown as distinct labeled pills; SWAP uses a lucide refresh icon.
Swap panel polish — each monster card now shows a 3px rarity-color strip at the bottom and an element-tinted border rim so you can read rarity and type at a glance.

Beast Showcase popup upgraded — close button uses a proper icon, the veteran badge uses a lucide medal, and stats are now shown as a 6-bar visual grid (HP/ATK/DEF/SpA/SpD/SPD) with color-coded fills, matching the Beastbook.
Expedition popup upgraded — swords icon, gold italic 'IN PROGRESS' kicker above the zone name, and VIEW/END buttons now show lucide icons alongside their labels.

Battles are now fully keyboard-playable — arrow keys move between FIGHT/SWITCH/BAG/CONTRACT/END, number keys 1-4 instantly fire a move, 1-3 pick a target, Q swaps and E opens the bag, Space confirms and Shift backs out. Every action and move shows its hotkey on a small key-cap right on the label. Mouse still works exactly as before.

Menus and popups are now keyboard-navigable too — arrow keys move the highlight, Space confirms, Shift backs out. Confirm dialogs, the menu popup, options, the shop, the world map, and the expedition result screen can all be driven without the mouse. Opening a popup hands it the keyboard so it never fights the screen underneath it.
Hard Mode can now actually be selected on the expedition team screen — the HARD pill showed as unlocked but clicking it only played a deny sound.
Beast gene totals were undercounting — the roster GENES value and gene-sort now count all six genes (Sp. Atk and Sp. Def were being left out).
Boss reward drops no longer include catch lures — catch items are shop-only.
Beasts revived between expedition waves no longer occasionally come back tilted from their KO collapse.
Confirming CONTRACT with the keyboard during battle no longer activates END instead — keyboard selection now always matches the highlighted action diamond.

Breeding panel now shows all six genes — the parent comparison table and the offspring gene-range preview were missing Sp. Atk and Sp. Def, and the gene-total cap read /200 instead of the correct /180.

Daily milestone rewards now unlock by total cumulative login days as intended — the claim button was wrongly gated on the consecutive streak, so anyone who missed a day could never claim the longer milestones even with the progress bar full.
The 'Supreme Tamer' achievement no longer unlocks early — it now correctly requires defeating all three expedition bosses, including the Loomweaver's Burrow mini-expedition boss.
Chat popup now moves smoothly while you drag it — previously the window only snapped to its new position when some unrelated update (a new message, a channel switch) happened to refresh the panel.
Game tabs now switch only with the number keys 1-6 — pressing WASD or the arrow keys no longer jumps you between tabs, so those keys stop interfering with panel and content navigation.

The bag is now fully keyboard-navigable — number keys 1-7 switch category tabs, WASD or arrows move the item cursor, Space uses the highlighted item, and Q closes the bag. The bag was also widened so the item grid fits comfortably.
The contract negotiation screen is now keyboard-navigable — 1-4 pick an approach, A/D step between them, Space attempts the contract, Tab toggles Master Ink, and Q cancels.
Help tab gains a Controls section — a full keyboard guide covering tab navigation, battle, taming, the bag, and popups so the keyboard map is discoverable in-game.
Keyboard 'confirm' across menus, battle, and popups is now consistently Space or Enter — it was previously also bound to the left mouse button action, which could double-fire a click.

Beasts roster keyboard navigation fixed — the detail panel now follows your keyboard selection instead of flickering the whole grid on every keypress, and W/S move exactly one row (they were jumping a fixed 5 cards regardless of how many actually fit per row).

Roster and Beastbook detail panels are now fully keyboard-operable — press Space on a beast to hand keyboard control to the detail panel, where the arrows move a cursor over every interactive control (the nickname pencil, the showcase/journal/favourite diamonds, the action buttons, and all four move slots in the Beasts panel). Space activates the highlighted control, the panel auto-scrolls to keep it on screen, and Q returns to the grid.

The bottom command bar's non-tab buttons now have keyboard shortcuts — 7 opens Quests, 8 the Menu, 9 the Bag, 0 your Profile, and T/R/C/N toggle Chat, Radio, Active Effects, and Notifications. Each button shows its key on a small gold key-cap, matching the 1-6 tab caps.

The in-game guide is now fully keyboard-navigable — W/S (or arrows) walk a single cursor through every topic and sub-page in one list, and the guide updates live as you move. Space starts reading (W/S then scroll the page), and Q steps back to the list, then closes the guide. The Controls section also now renders correctly — it was previously showing a blank page.
Beastbook keyboard navigation — W/S now move exactly one row instead of jumping a fixed 8 cards; the row size is measured from the live grid so it stays correct at any window width.

Shop keyboard navigation no longer jumps between categories — A/D and W/S now follow the on-screen order (the grid regroups items by category, but navigation had been walking the raw unsorted list), and W/S move to the item directly above or below across category section breaks.
Keyboard navigation in the My Beasts roster, Beastbook, and Shop now scrolls the grid to follow your selection — the highlighted card stays on screen instead of drifting out of view as you move.

The Embark / team-picker popup is now fully keyboard-operable — arrows or WASD move a visible cursor through your roster (it scrolls to follow), Space/Enter picks a beast, F auto-fills, C clears, 1/2/3 load or save team presets, the < and > keys cycle the element filter, R embarks and Q closes. Every action button shows its key on a small gold cap.
Heartwell's sprite refreshed with cleaner, updated art.

Full-roster moveset lore pass — one more sweep so every beast's moveset reads true to its body and personality. Embrik, the timid headless flame-foal with no claws, trades a 'brutal slash' for Cinder's Curse (its hollow ghost-flame). Pyrgard and Manehelm, loyal protector-knights, stop war-crying — they steel themselves with Forge Temper instead, and Manehelm swaps a 'primal roar' for an Ember Wall guard befitting a sentinel. Seraphiel, Aurael, and Wishstar drop wind 'talon/claw' moves they have no talons for (a serpent-armed seraph, a phantom-handed herald, a planet-bodied king) and pick up clean wind-cut and wind-slam moves instead. Liliprince the Weavermere pond-prince sheds an ocean-energy ward for a freshwater Aqua Shield. Lochmaw the deep-sea apex predator stops bracing and learns Dread Gaze — the deep waters part before it. Cerametz, the patient urn-sheep, stops going into a self-confusing Blossom Frenzy and lashes out with Wild Thorn instead.

Off-element move pass — beasts whose stories reach beyond their element now learn a move to match. Embrik, a foal born dead and animated by a borrowed flame, picks up the shadowy Shade Step. Pyrgard's forged burning helm gives it the steel-hard Iron Rush, foreshadowing Manehelm's Fire/Metal typing. Brooding dark-knight Gothsire learns the shadow-clawed Umbral Claw, foreshadowing Lochmaw's Water/Shadow turn. The warden-seraph Seraphiel blesses its silvered blade with Sacred Strike, and the crowned herald Aurael calls down Lunar Radiance — Spirit moves for an angelic line. And Twincoil's hexing inner face, the one whose eyes never blink, learns Dread Gaze.

The 'Perfection' achievement (fuse a beast with a perfect gene) can now actually be earned — it was checking for a gene value of 31, which is impossible since genes cap at 30, so the achievement was permanently unreachable.

The 'Beastborne Master' achievement (discover every species) no longer counts the retired AI-gen beasts that are hidden from the Beastbook and can't be encountered — completion now correctly tracks the handmade launch roster. The Beastbook completion counter and percentage display were also reading against the full hidden roster and now show the right numbers.

Fixed achievement rewards being silently lost — if you unlocked an achievement and quit before claiming it, the next login would mark it claimed without ever granting the reward. Unclaimed achievement rewards now reliably wait for you.
Boss-clear achievements ('Boss Slayer', 'Supreme Tamer') now unlock retroactively for players who defeated expedition bosses before these achievements existed.

The 'Point Hoarder' achievement (invest 100 skill points) now counts skill-point cost correctly when checking past progress — skills that cost more than 1 point per rank were being undercounted, so the achievement could fail to unlock for players who had genuinely spent enough.

Hard Mode expedition achievements reworded to match what they actually track — they unlock on the number of expeditions cleared on Hard Mode, in any order, so they're now 'Clear 1/2/3 expeditions on Hard Mode' (Hard Mode Initiate / Veteran / Master) instead of naming specific zones, which could mislead.

Shop Daily Spotlight card no longer shows the level-requirement lock floating loose under the discount badge — the lock now sits as a clean stacked pair directly beneath the '% OFF TODAY' badge, properly aligned and spaced.
Shop Daily Spotlight card's vertical divider hairline renders correctly again — a gradient quirk had collapsed it to an invisible sliver.
Radio widget's progress bar no longer overlaps the now-playing track card — it now sits below the card with a clean gap.

The Online tab is now keyboard-navigable — the < and > keys cycle between the Tamers, Leaderboards, and Guild sections, arrows or WASD move a cursor through the tamer tiles, Space/Enter opens a tamer's card in the sidebar, and the grid scrolls to keep your selection on screen.

The main menu is now fully keyboard-operable end to end — the open-beta greeting, the Now Hiring popup, the cloud-save-unreachable prompt, and the reset-data confirm all take the keyboard while open (arrows pick a button, Space confirms, Q backs out to the safe choice), and the Patch Notes panel scrolls with the arrow keys or the mouse wheel.
On-screen hotkey hints added across more panels — the Online hub, Shop, and Beastbook each show a hint for the keys that cycle sections, stores, and the element filter.
Cycling a panel's sections/stores/element filter no longer also skips the radio track — panel cycling moved to the < and > keys, leaving [ and ] as the dedicated radio track-skip shortcut.

Loading your save no longer falsely claims that offline progress was discarded on every boot — and when your local progress is more recent than the cloud (e.g. the last cloud sync didn't finish before you closed the game), that newer progress is now kept and synced up, instead of being silently replaced by a slightly older cloud copy.

The Leaderboards tab is now keyboard-navigable — A/D rotate the category-group carousel (Battle, Collection, Social, Economy), W/S move a cursor through the category cards, Space expands the focused card to the top 20, and F refreshes the boards.

The Guild panel is now fully keyboard-navigable — every view (landing, browse, the guild plaza, and the create-guild form) can be driven without the mouse. WASD or arrows move a cursor and Space confirms; in the guild plaza W/S flow straight down the whole screen — action tiles, announcement/description cards, roster, perks, danger zone — and A/D move sideways within a section. The Announcement and Description edit pencils and the full Guild Settings drawer are all keyboard-operable — arrows walk the setting rows, left/right or Space changes each one. The browse grid, perk list, and settings page scroll to keep your selection on screen, and every sub-panel — the member context menu, invite picker, and raid team select — takes the keyboard while open. Pending join requests sit inline at the top of the roster and are part of the same W/S walk: A/D pick ACCEPT or DENY on a request, Space fires it, and the REQUESTS chip jumps the cursor straight to the first request. Q backs out.

The bag's ALL ITEMS count now matches the items actually shown — old saves could carry ghost item IDs (typo'd daily-streak rewards like 'gene_booster' that should have been 'boss_gene_booster', plus stale material IDs from removed beasts) that inflated the badge total but never rendered. The header now filters to only items that can resolve, and the typo'd milestone reward IDs are corrected so future grants resolve to real items. Unresolvable IDs are kept in your save (not deleted) so that if a future patch adds the missing registration, those items reappear.

Fixed the entire UI rendering at the wrong size after the s&box 26.06.03 engine update — the CSS engine changed unitless line-height to a font-size multiplier, which ballooned every text element's line box and shoved the menu and panels out of place. All line-heights pinned to explicit pixel values; menus, battle, roster, shop, and every panel lay out correctly again.

Skill tree no longer drifts out of sync across sessions — a self-healing audit now runs on every login, level-up, and shop reset and quietly puts your skill points and invested ranks back in step if any prior corruption left them mismatched. The shop's 'Respec' button now also refunds the full cost-correct SP and actually clears the tree (the old respec was clearing a throwaway list and refunding only one rank per skill, regardless of how much you'd invested). Trees that were already healthy are left alone — no surprise wipes.

Fusion Complete is now a proper cinematic moment — the screen dims while a charge ring spins up, then a flash blooms as your new beast slams in on a column of light with its name. The gene table cascades in row by row showing each stat against both parents, and the quality and nature settle in last. The fuse payoff finally feels earned, not flat.

Signing a contract now lands like the catch it is — the 'Contract Signed!' panel slams in with a flash, the title punches in, and your new beast springs up from a burst of light and sparks instead of just fading on screen. The four approach diamonds also fan in left-to-right each time the contract screen opens.

Claiming an achievement reward now actually celebrates — a gold flash, an expanding shockwave ring, a 12-mote sparkle burst, and a center card that slams in naming what you earned, all timed so your currency ticks up right as the burst peaks. Claim All gets the same moment with a running count. The achievement list also now cascades in row by row each time you open the panel or switch categories instead of appearing all at once.

Claiming your Day 7 streak reward is now a full-screen moment — the room dims and an iris ring contracts, then your Master Ink slams up a pillar of light, a gold-and-purple name banner punches in with god-rays and confetti, and your currency ticks up right as the celebration peaks. Routine daily claims stay quick and snappy, so the seventh day actually feels like the payoff it is.

Expedition screen feels like an event now — the team-select view assembles itself with a staggered slide-in (header, then roster, then your team panel cascading top to bottom) every time you open it, and clearing a zone fires a green 'ZONE CLEARED' burst with a light-ray sweep and expanding spark ring before the rewards screen lands.

Arena win screens now celebrate the big moments — climbing a rank tier fires a gold 'RANK UP' flash with your old rank arrowing up into the new one, and hitting a win-streak milestone (3, 5, 10, 15+) drops a full-screen moment: the screen dims, god-rays and shockwaves bloom, and your streak number slams in flanked by flames. Earned through wins, not luck.

Completing a trade now lands like a real exchange — a green flash, twin shockwave rings, a sparkle burst, and rotating light-rays bloom behind a 'TRADE COMPLETE' card that slams in, with a layered success-and-reward chime. The incoming trade-request popup also got a polish pass: its gold icon spins in, the title/message/buttons stagger up, and the Accept/Decline buttons now press in when you click them.

Discovering a new species now gets a proper moment in the Beastbook — when you contract a beast you've never recorded, a full-screen 'NEW SPECIES DISCOVERED' reveal blooms: the screen dims, light rings and rays sweep out behind the beast as it springs in, and its name slams up with a sparkle burst, tinted to its rarity. The Beastbook grid also deals its cards in on open, and selecting a beast now cascades its detail page into view instead of snapping.

Main menu rebuilt as a launcher hub — a frosted left sidebar (logo, big gold PLAY block, Roadmap/Options/Patch Notes nav, Discord card) alongside a featured update card with live event pill, headline art, and quick Roadmap/Community shortcuts. Reads like a live-service launcher and surfaces what's new the moment you boot.

Main menu color + life pass — the featured card now reads as a raised, lit-from-above surface with a breathing rim glow, the PLAY button carries a slow gold sheen and breathing halo to draw the eye, and the Roadmap and Community cards each picked up their own identity (teal-blue for Roadmap, Discord blurple for Community) with a glowing accent edge and lift on hover. The OUT NOW stamp wiggles, the purple backdrop drifts, and the whole menu feels alive instead of flat.

Main menu no longer shows two things lit at once — when you switch from the mouse to the keyboard, the Play Now / Patch Notes buttons and the Roadmap/Community cards drop their mouse-hover glow immediately, leaving only the keyboard selection. Move the mouse and hover comes right back.

Main menu keyboard navigation is now fully 2D — WASD (or arrows) move the violet selection in every direction, so you can press D from the sidebar to reach the Play Now / Patch Notes buttons and the Roadmap / Community cards on the right, which were previously unreachable by keyboard. LANGUAGE and QUIT now sit as a left/right pair (D goes to QUIT, A back to LANGUAGE).

Main menu Roadmap & Community cards redesigned — instead of repeating the sidebar, the Roadmap card now previews what's in development (Tower Mode, Ranked Battling) and the Community card shows live Discord presence with the real member count pulled straight from Discord.

Roadmap popup redesigned as 'What We're Building' — a clean 3×2 grid of feature cards (Tower Mode and Ranked Battling marked IN DEVELOPMENT with a violet accent, the rest COMING UP), a live OPEN BETA status pill, and a footer that invites you to send feedback or join the Discord.

Main menu now renders in the game's italic display type throughout — titles, nav, and body copy all carry the Beastborne slant (the italic font face is now actually loaded in-engine instead of silently falling back to upright).

Open-beta welcome popup redesigned to match the refined menu — a two-line title, flask icon badge, cleaner copy that invites suggestions, improvements, and feature ideas (not just bug reports), a single Got It button with a violet focus ring, and a smooth pop-up / pop-down animation. The Roadmap popup's Send Feedback button now opens the in-game feedback panel.
Main menu selection is now a single 'living' cursor — one violet ring that glides and liquid-stretches between options as you hover or arrow around, instead of each option lighting up in place.

Main menu right panel cleanup — the Community card's Join button and divider line no longer get clipped off the right edge, and the featured Update card's right edge now lines up flush with the Roadmap/Community cards below it on a matching angle (it previously leaned in steeper since it's a wider card).

Main menu now tilts into the screen for real depth — the sidebar buttons, the featured Update card, and the Roadmap/Community cards all recede on a consistent 3D angle, with the two bottom cards reading as one continuous receding surface.

Selecting a sidebar option (Roadmap / Options / Patch Notes) now fills it with a solid dark slab behind the label, ringed by the violet living cursor — and the fill has a gentle liquid motion of its own that plays against the ring, so the selection feels alive.

Main menu has a brand-new animated wave background — a custom looping animation now fills the whole backdrop, replacing the old static pattern, the faint purple bokeh video, and the drifting light beam.

The PLAY button's gold surface is now liquid — it gently undulates like the menu's selection fills while the label stays steady. The hazy gold glows behind PLAY, Play Now, and View are gone; everything reads crisper against the animated wave backdrop.

Main menu sidebar leans deeper into the screen, and selecting any option now makes the button itself lunge toward you — PLAY and the nav rows pop out of the 3D lean with a slight swell, and the Discord card and footer buttons slide with the selection, with the violet living cursor riding along perfectly.

Options panel rebuilt in the game's new solid-slab look — the thin grey outlines on every row, toggle, and card are gone, each section now carries a colored edge bar and matching gem, toggles and buttons snap instantly to hover and press, and Done is now a proper gold button.

Main menu de-cluttered into clean color-block shapes — the thin outlines around the event pill, featured card, bottom cards, IN DEV chips, Patch Notes button, and sidebar edge are gone; the Discord card now wears a blurple edge bar like the big cards, and idle buttons sit darker so the thing you're pointing at is clearly the brightest.

Clicking PLAY now fires the transition instead of waiting for it — the button squashes and snaps back, the violet cursor slams shut around it in gold, a flash blooms off the button, and a gold streak shoots across the screen to summon the wipe.

Main menu entrance rebuilt — the featured card and bottom cards now deal in along their 3D angle while the sidebar options cascade in one after another, and the whole menu is interactive about half a second sooner.

The featured update card now takes on its beast's element — a fire, water, or wind tint on the kicker bar, top-edge shine, and backdrop, changing with the rotating featured art. Gold stays reserved for the buttons.
Splash text is back — the line under the menu logo now stamps in fresh from a 50-deep rotation on every visit instead of always reading 'Genetics go brrrrr.'

Pressing PLAY now properly detonates — the button squashes and pops, the selection ring slams shut in gold, a thick white-hot bolt fires across the screen, and the whole screen flashes gold for a beat as the wipe sweeps in.

Roadmap, Options, and Patch Notes no longer pop up over the menu — they slide in as a tall panel from the right edge while the menu dims behind them, with their content cascading in. Click the dim, press Q, or hit the X to slide them away.
The menu's Options panel got roomier — bigger rows, a short description under every section header, and sections that cascade in when it opens. The in-game Options popup is unchanged.

Auto-Contract is now smart — instead of a fixed strategy, it looks at every approach offered for the beast in front of it and uses the one with the best success odds it can afford. The fixed Generous/Fair/Strict/Golden picker is gone, and the contract screen now pre-selects that same best approach when it opens.

Roadmap, Options, and Patch Notes are now full scene swaps — clicking one makes the whole menu fly off along its 3D angle (your clicked button hanging on a beat longer) and the new screen deals in on an angled backdrop slab, with the violet cursor gliding across to it. Q or X flies you back the same way, faster. No more side drawer.
Selecting the Roadmap or Community card on the main menu now lights up the whole card — the colored edge bar flares wider and the card lifts — instead of only the little View/Join pill reacting.

Roadmap, Patch Notes and Options screens redesigned to use the full screen — the Roadmap is now a big two-column feature grid, Patch Notes gets a version-and-contents rail beside a wide reading column, and Options lays its sections out in two columns.

Visible keyboard shortcuts across the menu screens — key caps show Q to go back, A/D to move the selection ring, Enter to select, W/S to scroll, and number keys to fire the footer actions directly. Full mouse + keyboard parity everywhere.
The main menu no longer flashes back into view for a split second while flying off to the Roadmap, Options, or Patch Notes screens.
The violet selection ring now lands on the new screen's close button after a scene swap instead of stranding over empty space.
Roadmap and Patch Notes headers no longer fuse their title words together ('What We'reBuilding'), and the Balance & Economy roadmap card finally shows its icon.

Opening Roadmap, Options, or Patch Notes from the main menu no longer freezes for a beat with the old menu stuck on screen — the angled backdrop now sweeps in from the very start of its flight instead of popping in part-way through.

Roadmap rebuilt as a 3-poster marquee — Tower Mode, Story, and Bug Fixing each get a big poster with a colored gem, a slanted status stamp (IN DEVELOPMENT pulses live), and one line of copy instead of a wall of text. Hover or focus a poster and it snaps to attention; Enter opens Send Feedback.

Each menu screen now has its own color voice and lean — Roadmap gold, Patch Notes violet (its backdrop tilts the OTHER way), Options teal — with a signature strip that draws itself in on every arrival. Headers across all three went big: 52px display titles, a 64px version number on Patch Notes, poster-size category headings.
A/D now walks every focusable on the Roadmap and Patch Notes screens — and pushing past either end flies you straight between the two scenes, no menu detour. The footer key caps show the way.

The violet selection ring no longer strands over a dead menu button after opening Roadmap or Patch Notes — scene controls now self-heal their focus targets even if the screen rebuilt under the cursor.

Options gains an Audio section — Master, UI, and Music volume each get a 0–100% control that applies instantly and is remembered between sessions (the radio widget's volume slider now remembers too). Gameplay also picks up two new toggles: Screen Shake (turn off battle camera shake entirely) and the smart Auto-Contract, finally settable from Options. A/D adjust the volume rows from the keyboard.
Removed the Options panel's 'coming soon' Accessibility rows — no more settings that look real but do nothing. They'll return when they actually work.

Roadmap and Patch Notes screens refined — new prev/next arrow buttons on the screen edges for switching scenes with the mouse (A/D still cycles, and the arrows wear the key caps), a much bigger close button, the footer bar removed so the posters and notes get the room, each poster/section accent now underlines its title and flares wider on hover, and all the cards now sweep in and out with the angled backdrop instead of just fading.

Confirm dialogs ('Release this beast?', 'Leave this guild?', etc.) rebuilt on the game's new button language — solid red or gold action buttons with italic display labels, a quiet dark Cancel, and the violet ring cursor marking your keyboard selection instead of the old glow.

Experimental PHONE LAUNCHER — press 8 (or the MENU button) to summon a phone-shaped app grid with every destination as its own color-coded app. Tapping an app floods the screen with that app's color and drops you straight into it. The bottom bar still works exactly as before while we trial the two side-by-side.

Phone launcher v2 — the grid now looks like a real phone home screen: each destination is a solid color-filled app icon with its label underneath, the phone itself is bigger, the backdrop properly dims the game behind it, and launching an app now sweeps an angled slab of that app's color across the screen (in and out in under half a second) instead of the old expanding circle.
The phone has a name — meet the PawPad, running TamerLink OS.
The main menu's living violet cursor now lives on the PawPad too — one ring that glides between app icons with the same liquid lean, instead of a static highlight popping tile to tile.
PawPad layout no longer drifts right — app labels and their key caps sit centered under their icons, and the clock, tamer line, and PROTOTYPE stamp stay inside the phone's edge.

PawPad glow-up — the phone now slides in at the right side of the screen (angled toward you, game still visible behind a lighter dim), apps lift toward you on hover with the violet ring riding along, keycaps sit on each icon's corner, and the top gets a proper phone treatment: signal bars, your Steam avatar by your name, a TAMERLINK OS header with a gold underline, and an energy hairline along the device's edge. The PROTOTYPE stamp is gone.
Launching Beasts, Skills, Shop, and the other main apps from the PawPad now actually plays the color sweep transition — a stale-data bug was silently making every app open like a plain popup toggle.

The PawPad now looks like an actual device — a proper bezel wraps the screen with a speaker slit, camera dot, and side buttons on its edge. The glowing top hairline and the gold underline in the header are gone, app labels sit dead-center under their icons, and the WASD/ENTER/Q hint caps at the bottom render properly instead of wrapping or showing up blank.

Opening the PawPad no longer tanks the frame rate — an always-on animation was forcing the whole tilted phone to redraw every frame. The phone also now reliably slides fully on-screen instead of occasionally stranding as a sliver at the right edge.

PawPad polish round — the violet cursor got its liquid wobble back and now centers exactly on every app icon, your Steam avatar shows up beside your name, a gold paw mark sits by the PawPad wordmark, and the hard-to-read key hints at the bottom are gone (each icon's corner keycap has you covered).

The PawPad got a commissioned icon set — every app now wears a custom hand-drawn glyph (a chunky paw for Beasts, a skill gem, a compass, a paw-emblem tome, and more) instead of generic line icons, plus a new System Dock row at the bottom with quick access to your Profile, Settings, the Guide, and Feedback.

PawPad apps now sit flat on the glass like a real phone — hover one and it lifts off with a colored shadow planted beneath it, and launching an app sends its icon rocketing off ahead of the color sweep. The cursor ring's liquid motion got richer too — it breathes and flexes instead of just leaning side to side.
PawPad icons come alive when you hover them — the paw taps, the bell swings, the chat dots type, the gem glints. Every app and dock icon has a looping animation that plays while highlighted.

The PawPad got its final hardware design — a graphite titanium body with gold trim, a real speaker and gold-ringed camera in the bezel, a gold power key, a debossed paw on the chin, and a layered wallpaper with drifting geometry and a ghost paw watermark. The status bar now shows gold signal bars, a battery, and your name beside a gold-ringed avatar.

Chat redesigned in the new look — a slanted chat-blue CHAT seam up top, GLOBAL/GUILD/TRADE as angled chips, a bigger window with cleaner unboxed messages (your own messages carry a blue edge), italic author names, and a blue send button that wears the violet ring on hover. Still draggable by the header, still toggles with T.

Expedition prep redesigned as a field briefing — the world map wears a big expedition-orange header with your zone-clear progress, zone briefings open with a tilted recommended-level stamp and a 5-diamond THREAT rating, and the embark popup now has the NORMAL/HARD toggle right next to the button (hard mode was previously unreachable from the live flow — the level readout, stamp, and EMBARK button all go red when you arm it). The living violet ring now marks whatever zone, beast, or team slot you're pointing at, team slots show bigger sprites with two-tone element badges, and the whole flow stays fully keyboard-playable.

My Beasts rebuilt around your beast, not the list — the selected beast now owns a big stage on the left with its sprite at twice the size over a rarity-colored pedestal, species kicker above a big italic name, gold LV and PWR stamps, and the full dossier (actions, stats, moves, traits) laid out with room to breathe, while your collection becomes a scanning rail on the right under the filters. The living violet ring still glides card-to-card, a TAB/Q hint on the stage shows how to hand the keyboard between grid and stage, and fusion, multi-release, filters, and every hotkey work exactly as before.

The PawPad becomes a real phone - Chat, Radio, Effects, and Alerts now open ON the phone screen as TamerLink OS apps (channel tabs, live messages and typing, radio transport controls, buff and alert lists) instead of separate popups. Tap an app or use its hotkey while the phone is open.

The PawPad now sits flat and faces you straight-on - easier to read and type on now that real apps live on it - and the whole bottom command bar is retired: your player tag (avatar, level, currencies) lives in the bottom-left corner and the PawPad button in the bottom-right, leaving the full screen to the game.

The Bag rebuilt as a full-screen field satchel — category pouch tabs run down the left spine (with their 1-7 key caps), search leads the tools row, items spread across a roomier grid with bigger art and NEW stamps on fresh pickups, and inspecting an item floats a card on the right with a big gold USE button. The living violet ring now glides between items as you navigate, and everything stays fully keyboard-playable (1-7 tabs, WASD cursor, Space use, Q close).

The Shop rebuilt as a market stall — goods now stand big on shelf runs with price gems hanging under them (no more cramped card boxes), and a gold-trimmed display case on the right showcases the Daily Spotlight by default and whatever you pick up from the counter, with the quantity picker, sale prices, and one big gold BUY button always in the same spot. Gold Market and Boss Exchange are big angled signboards up top, the living violet ring glides between goods as you browse, and every hotkey works as before (< > swap stores, WASD browse, Enter buys).

The Beastbook rebuilt as a museum wall — one species now commands a giant center-stage exhibit (huge animated sprite over a teal-lit pedestal with its registry number watermarked behind), the species index shrinks to a compact slot rail on the left crowned by your completion count as a big hero stat, and the full reading — name, elements, rarity, flavor, stats, moves, lore, mastery — lives on a gallery placard at the right, with the evolution line drawn as connected diamond nodes showing the level each evolution happens. The living violet ring glides slot-to-slot as you browse, the book opens straight onto your first beast instead of an empty page, and every key works as before (WASD browse, Z/X element cycle, Space to the placard, Q back).

Quest log rebuilt as a full-screen notice board — quests are pinned slips laid out two across (twice as many visible at once), anything claimable sorts to the top and sits flat with a gold pin and a pulsing gold CLAIM button while in-progress slips rest at a slight tilt, rewards hang off each slip as gem tags, finished quests settle flat under a green DONE stamp, and the daily streak lives on its own pinned calendar card. The old side rail is gone — tabs and the reset timer share one slim quest-green header.

Online hub redesigned around presence — a TamerLink-blue header with big angled TAMERS/LEADERBOARDS tabs replaces the old pill row, online tamers show as clean presence cards (avatar in their title color, name, gold LV slab, a YOU chip on your own card) with the living violet ring gliding between them as you navigate, and the leaderboards trade their medal stamps for gold/silver/bronze rank diamonds with your own row highlighted in blue and the A/D · W/S · Space · F keys shown right on the board.

The system screens now match the PawPad they launch from — your Tamer Card leads with a big gold-ringed avatar (arena record tucked into a quiet strip until PvP goes live), the Game Guide gets dock-style topic tiles with its W/S · SPACE · Q keys shown right in the header (and its controls pages updated for the retired bottom bar), Feedback gets a warm composer with one gold SEND, and the system menu is a clean centered list with the living violet ring gliding between entries.

My Beasts ground-up style unification — the whole page now speaks one language: the 45° diamond motif is retired (actions, moves, and pickers use clean icon-tile slabs with element-colored edges), the dossier sections sit on one open stage surface instead of nested gray boxes, Quality/Nature/Traits become color-edged tiles, the XP bar is a real gold gauge with its numbers inside, the filter dropdowns (here and in the Beastbook) are angled slabs matching the header, and the panel's own paw glyph now drifts as a living background behind everything.
Favorite a beast straight from the collection rail — hover any card and tap the star in its corner, no more select-then-star round trip. The star stays lit on favorites.

One cursor everywhere on My Beasts — when you Tab into the beast's dossier, the same living violet ring that rides the collection now wraps whichever control the keyboard is on (actions, move slots, pickers), replacing the old gold-border highlight.

Beast collection cards redesigned in the new look — rounder solid slabs that let the sprite own the card, an angled LV chip, element badges on raised glyph tiles beside the name, rarity shown as a small skewed pedestal under the beast's feet, and a quieter recess for empty slots. Hover and selection now read as clean color shifts with the violet ring carrying the cursor, so nothing fights the pixel art — the same card style follows into the team picker, fusion, and trading screens.

The Beasts page is rebuilt from scratch as Center Stage — three zones: your collection as a card rail on the left, the selected beast standing HUGE (2.5×) center-stage on a slate floor with its name, level, XP gauge, element tags, and actions right under it, and a facts dossier (stats, quality, traits, moves, info, journal) scrolling on the right. Fusion turns the stage into an altar where both parents flank the predicted offspring, multi-release docks its confirm bar under the stage, and the living violet ring plus every hotkey follow you across all three zones.

Every major page now has a living background — each screen's own app glyph (shop, bag, quests, skills, online, Beastbook, beasts) drifts slowly across the dark backdrop at the house angle, replacing the old static fills. Subtle, always in motion, and each page wears its own icon.

Contract negotiation redesigned in the new look — the four approaches are now angled two-tone tiles fanned over the beast (big violet odds chip, name, costs, and their 1-4 keycaps on each), with a CONTRACT OFFER banner, the personality hint on a clean slab, and a beast dossier (sprite with element edge, level, your ink, the Master Ink toggle) above one big gold ATTEMPT. Signing still bursts — the beast's name now headlines its own celebration card with a bigger portrait.

Expedition results redesigned — the end-of-run popup is now a clean dark card with an angled EXPEDITION COMPLETE/FAILED banner, a solid victory (or defeat) diamond, rewards as their own gold-lit rows, and the game's standard gold/dark buttons with the violet ring marking your keyboard selection.

Trading redesigned in the new look — the trade table is now one big rounded slab in TamerLink blue with an italic TRADE masthead, your beasts show as the new roster-style cards (violet hover, blue selected, green when offered), READY UP is a proper gold slab that turns green once you lock in, and the incoming trade request arrives as a clean blue-chip popup with a gold ACCEPT.

Beast Showcase and Tamer Card popups rebuilt as proper show-off cards — the shared beast now stands big center-stage on its own slab with its element as a base strip and its POWER in big gold italics, and the Tamer Card leads with a gold-ringed avatar, a gold level number, and your lifetime record up top (the arena strip waits quietly below until PvP goes live).

Tutorial refreshed for new players — the walkthrough now reads off calm dark cards with a violet TUTORIAL chip, bigger body text, SPACE / Q key hints shown right on the card, and action hints arrive on a quieter banner that stays out of the way of what it's pointing at.
Credits screen restyled to match the new system menus — dark slab, violet section bars, and a gold version chip.

Achievements redesigned in the new system-slab look — angled category chips that light up in their category's color, a completion keycap in the header, two-tone entry tiles (gold-lit when a reward is ready, quiet green check once claimed, dimmed while locked), and every CLAIM button now wears the game's standard gold. The claim celebration and cascading list entrance stay.

The daily login popup now speaks the same language as the Quests page — the 7-day strip uses the same green/gold day tiles (green check when claimed, pulsing gold ring on today, Day 7 gold-washed with its MASTER INK stamp), your streak number goes big gold italic, mission rows become clean two-tone tiles with green progress bars, and one big gold CLAIM REWARD carries the moment. The Day-7 cinematic is untouched.

The developer Gift Inbox got the system-popup treatment — a clean dark slab with a violet FROM THE DEVELOPERS chip, each gift on its own tile with your loot in gold italics, and a single big gold CLAIM ALL.

Beastbook refinement pass — the index rail's specimen thumbs now frame every beast cleanly in identical tiles (art offsets were tuned for the old big cards and threw sprites out of frame), the showcase spotlight is a soft teal glow instead of a hard disc-and-bar pedestal, element tags on a beast's page went big and skewed to match the Beasts stage, and undiscovered species now get a real registry page — their number, an UNDISCOVERED stamp, a silhouette, and FIELD NOTES that name the actual zones where the beast can be sighted.
Beasts page gains a RECORD section — every beast's dossier now shows its lifetime battle ledger: knockouts, total damage dealt, bosses felled, and expeditions completed.

Beasts page moves list rebuilt — each of the four moves is now a full-width card with its description, accuracy, PP, and effects written right on it. The flickery hover tooltip is gone; everything it said is just visible now.
Beasts page ACTIONS row no longer hangs off the right side of its section — the ITEM / FUSE / RELEASE slabs now sit centered under the stage.

Beasts page feels alive — switching beasts pops the sprite onto the stage and cascades the dossier sections in one after another, the spotlight under the beast slowly breathes, stat and XP bars sweep to their new values on every switch, and the action buttons light their icon tiles on hover and press in on click.

Beasts page readability pass — the stage and dossier now read as one joined inspection panel (color split kept, gap gone), the XP gauge is taller with its readout properly centered, dossier text got a size bump across stats, traits, and info, the quality tile gains a gene-total gauge, and Journal + Show Off sit side by side.

Beast Journal modernized — the diary popup now matches the game's current look: solid dark slabs, a violet JOURNAL chip with your beast's name in big italics, and each memory on a two-tone tile with a color-coded icon square and stamp badge instead of emoji.

The beast dossier is rebuilt as an angled ledger — a tilted FIELD DOSSIER lid caps the column, every section sits on its own slate with slanted lit-and-shadowed top and bottom edges that alternate lean down the stack, section titles ride the angled rooflines, and lineage folds into the info slate. The whole right panel reads like stacked slates with real depth instead of flat cards.

Beast dossier redesigned to the approved 'Signature Edge' look — one quiet panel where each section leads with a slanted violet header chip and a hairline rule; stats read as clean single-line rows with slim angled gauges; traits, moves, records, and the Journal/Show Off buttons become quiet cards with a signature clipped top-right corner; move slabs pick up violet effect chips (like '30% Paralyze') and angled gold STAB stamps.

My Beasts gains real scrollbars — both the collection grid and the dossier column now show a slim violet thumb along their right edge that tracks your scroll position and brightens when you mouse over the column.

The My Beasts header is alive — two soft violet waves drift through the band in opposite directions, endlessly, in collection AND Gene Forge mode alike (fusion wears the same violet as the rest of the beasts app now). Every page header will get its own accent waves over time.

Your selected beast now stands on an element dais — a soft elliptical stage glowing in its primary element's color (teal for Wind, orange for Fire, pink for Spirit...), replacing the flat violet spotlight circle.

The Learn Move picker now speaks the dossier's card language — each move is a full card with its element tile, gold STAB stamp, colored power token, description, and violet effect chip. Learning is a deliberate two-step: click a move to arm it (the card rings violet with a LEARN button), click again to confirm — no more accidental one-click move swaps.
Dossier numerals got louder — battle record numbers now stamp in a heavier upright display weight, and the six stat values sit a half-step bigger.

The Beast Journal is no longer a popup — it opens right inside the dossier column as a milestone timeline: boss trophies with the defeated boss's portrait in a medallion, evolutions showing both forms side by side in your beast's element color, max-level and name-change milestones, and 'The Beginning' always closing the story. The grind stats stay in RECORD; the journal keeps the big moments.
Renaming a beast is now remembered — the journal logs every name change with the old name beside the new one.

The dossier's sub-views each got a living header band — the Journal twinkles with faint starlight, the move picker has purple motes drifting upward, and the Gene Forge shows two violet orbs slowly orbiting each other, about to become one.

The corner menu phone got a proper glow-up — violet-rimmed body with a real screen inset, camera notch, and paw glyph, sitting in a soft purple corner glow that lifts it off busy screens. Notification badge now rides the corner with a clean dark ring.

Moving around My Beasts feels reactive now — opening the journal or a move picker fades its header band in and cascades the cards with a soft page-turn cue, journal milestones reveal one by one with The Beginning landing last, switching beasts flares the element dais and re-stamps the name and badges, arming a move flashes its ring as the LEARN button pops in, and every button in the panel presses in when clicked.

Keyboard navigation in My Beasts got its own life — the focused control now wears a clear violet cursor edge that flashes softly on every hop, the collection grid glides (instead of jumping) to keep your selection on screen, and pressing W at the top of the dossier scrolls all the way up so the stats are reachable without a mouse.

My Beasts is now fully playable on keyboard with one coherent map — D off the grid's right edge walks straight into the beast's page and A walks back out, Q means BACK everywhere (including the Gene Forge — R is now the fuse key, capped right on the FUSE button), the release confirmations finally answer to the keyboard (A/D picks Cancel or Release, starting safely on Cancel, Q backs out), W/S scrolls the journal, and a small key legend at the stage's foot shows the live shortcuts whenever you're driving by keyboard.

Keyboard and mouse highlights in My Beasts no longer fight — the panel tracks which device you used last, so moving the mouse instantly quiets the keyboard cursor and any key press brings it right back, with your dossier cursor position remembered per beast. A parked cursor can't keep buttons lit while you keyboard (even a tiny mouse twitch hands control back to the mouse), and keyboard scrolling no longer spams hover blips when rows slide under a resting pointer.

One cursor to rule My Beasts — hovering a card now moves the selection itself, with the liquid ring gliding to whatever you point at (the beast page follows a beat behind so fast sweeps stay smooth), and the same violet cursor edge follows your mouse or keyboard through the dossier, pickers, and confirm dialogs. The extra hover outline that used to double up with the ring is gone.

Fusion now lives entirely in the page — no more popup. The fuse cinematic plays over the altar while the two parents visibly drain from their slots, the offspring springs up right where the ? was with its name and quality stamped beneath, and the gene table rolls out in the right column comparing every gene against both parents (green where the roll beat their average). VIEW BEAST walks you straight to it in your collection; FUSE AGAIN reloads the forge (Q does too).

Fusion now wears the My Beasts violet — the selection ring, gene ledger chip, altar slots, B1/B2 tags, the FUSE button itself, and even the scrollbars all carry the same violet as the rest of the beasts app while you're fusing (they're the same app on your PawPad, after all).

My Beasts feel pass — buttons now rest brighter and press darker (hover dims a step, press dims two: a proper tactile ladder), the ITEM/FUSE/RELEASE row no longer flickers through rainbow border colors on hover, releasing beasts fades them out of the grid before it closes ranks, the release confirms slide in with a dim wash instead of popping, the dossier column scrolls with the same glide as the grid, PWR counts up to its new value on every switch, favorite stars pop when toggled, and release marks and B1/B2 tags flash as they land.

Fusing is now THE LOOM — threads of light unspool from both parents and weave into a rising two-tone helix, element color crossing forge violet, a bright shuttle spiraling up the strands; the risen weave contracts into a cocoon around the offspring's silhouette, pulses like a heartbeat in near-silence, and burns open in a violet flare as your new beast springs to life, centered on the forge. The result ledger then rolls out beat by beat, ending on VIEW BEAST / FUSE AGAIN.

Buttons across My Beasts now physically lift when you hover them and press down when you click — and inside the scrolling lists, where things can't move, the focused card's top edge catches the light instead.

The fusion ritual now weaves a REAL double helix — two glowing strands (your beast's element crossing forge violet) twist and rotate in 3D as they rise out of the gathering threads, and the whole ritual now fills the center column: the helix towers through the forge before contracting into the cocoon, and the reveal flare washes the full column.

FUSION GRID — cross-species fusion arrives at the forge. The fusion screen's right column is a grid of square tiles, one per fusion in the game: results you've recorded in your Beastbook show their sprite, name, and the level they'd come out at with your best eligible pair; results you've never seen appear as a dark silhouette with ??? — something to chase. Highlight a tile to see its recipe; click it to spotlight every eligible parent in your collection. Woven fusions carry a green check, and the first time you make a new one its tile flashes gold. Same-species fusion is always the first tile.

Fixed every keybind going dead on the Skill tree page — opening (or clicking anywhere on) the redesigned Skills tab silently captured the keyboard, killing WASD, Space, the phone (M), and even the 1-6 tab keys game-wide until you left the page. All keys work everywhere again.
The Skill tree's selection ring now centers properly on skill nodes instead of hugging their top-left corner.

Full keyboard support on the fusion screen — WASD walks the parent grid, E switches which slot you're filling, R confirms the fuse, and the new fusion tile grid is fully navigable: D off the grid (or Tab) crosses into the tiles, WASD moves in 2D with the column scrolling smoothly to follow, Space spotlights a fusion, and Q backs out. After a fuse, A/D pick VIEW BEAST / FUSE AGAIN and Q jumps straight back into the forge.

Keyboard walk-up to the My Beasts header — press W from the grid's top row and the selection ring climbs onto the filter/sort bar (element, rarity, genes, sort direction, and the FUSE / MULTI RELEASE / CANCEL buttons); A/D move across, Space clicks, S drops back into the grid. Works in fusion mode too.
The fusion result now fits on screen in one piece — reveal sprite, the full gene table, traits, and both buttons are all visible at once instead of scrolling inside the forge column.

E now works as a quiet alternate confirm alongside Space in panel navigation (skill tree, roster, fusion, pickers, result screens) — one-handed WASD+E play. Space remains the advertised key; E stays silent on the legends. Where E already means something (fusion slot-switch), that meaning wins.
Keyboard scrolling in My Beasts now glides — the dossier column and the fusion tile grid ease smoothly to keep your selection in view instead of snapping instantly to the top or bottom.

My Beasts action buttons (ITEM / FUSE / EVOLVE / RELEASE) now show the same accent-colored stroke whether you reach them by keyboard or mouse, and the stroke snaps straight to its color instead of flashing purple first.

Notifications now live on your PawPad — every alert lands in the phone's ALERTS app permanently (with a CLEAR ALL control), and the old floating popups are replaced by brief 'peeks' that slide out beside the phone, announce themselves with a little chip pop, and tuck back in after a few seconds. Click a peek (or press N) to open the phone straight to your alerts.

The Gene Forge reacts to everything you do now — slotting a parent makes its altar slot settle under the weight while the empty partner slot breathes an invitation, the offspring preview flashes awake with its chevrons snapping inward the moment a pair goes fusable, and the FUSE button glows with a slow breath when it's ready. Spotlighting a fusion sweeps a violet light-up wave across your eligible beasts column by column.

Fusion reveal choreography actually plays now — the offspring springs in, its name slides up, the quality stamp SLAMS down oversized with a recoil, and the gene ledger ticks its rows in one by one against both parents, with your rolled gene total counting up live and the LUCKY / ON TARGET / HARSH verdict landing only after the number settles. (A timing-engine quirk had been skipping the whole sequence and popping everything in at once.)

Fusion ritual feel pass — the gathering threads now snap taut with a little overshoot as they land, the cocoon's heartbeat thumps with real recoil weight, the helix rises on a smoother cinematic curve, the shell gets pulled in on a heavier collapse, and the final burst rips outward as a white-hot core ring inside the violet shockwave. First-time fusions also ping a discovery chime as their tile flashes gold, and the woven ✓ pops onto the tile mid-flash.
My Beasts dossier ripples on beast switch — trait cards and the four record tiles now cascade in one after another instead of appearing with their section all at once.

More hover life across My Beasts and the forge — fusion tiles deepen their art frame and light their name under the cursor, the nature/trait chips on slotted parents lift to meet you, and tiles acknowledge your click with a press-down.

The Beastbook is now the Specimen Hall — the page fully wears its teal: a living wave header, the selected beast standing on a glass display field with a fine measuring ring, a slanted registry nameplate with its number and name (undiscovered species show an empty display case and a '???' plate), and mastery now ranked in bronze/silver/gold medals instead of borrowing rarity colors. The detail column trades its rounded cards for the game's corner-cut slabs, move types show as dark badges with bright element rims, hovering the index rail selects instantly, and R cycles the element filter.

Trait effects are now written right on the panel instead of a broken hover popup — the fusion result lists each inherited trait with its effect and which parent it came from, and the trait/nature chips on slotted fusion parents no longer carry the misfiring tooltip (their full effect text lives in the beast's dossier).

The Beastbook's reading column now matches the My Beasts dossier — sections lead with the same slanted teal header chips and hairlines, stats use the same slanted gauges with big italic values, moves are full-width cards with their type's color on the edge, and the column scrolls with the same smooth glide and slim scrollbar. Trait effects are written directly on each trait instead of hiding behind a hover popup.

Beastbook beast pages rebuilt from the ground up — the name, number, and type/rarity tags now read as one clean registry block; the five actions are a labeled key row (no more mystery diamonds with hover tooltips) with the move count right on the MOVES key; the evolution line reads top-to-bottom as sprite medallions with 'BASE FORM' / 'FROM LV n' under each stage and a VIEWING tag on the one you're reading; lore entries and the mastery ladder wear their bronze/silver/gold ranks on cleaner rows, with mastery progress on the same slanted gauge the stats use.
Terra Force and Tidal Wrath trait icons no longer render blank — they were pointing at icon names that don't exist; Terra Force now shows a mountain and Tidal Wrath a storm surge.

The Online tab landed a full redesign — one page now shows everything at a glance: a BATTLE board with your rank badge and win/loss record (online battles themselves arrive in a coming update), live leaderboard standings with your row always pinned (R cycles the category), a trade board listing tamers you can trade with right now, your guild's banner and weekly goal, and a row of who's online — click any head for their profile. Fully keyboard-driven: WASD walks the page, Z/X hop between boards, Space or E confirms.

Online hub: the landing now wears the house look — filled slab zones with skewed blue section chips and corner cuts instead of thin outlined boxes, proper filled buttons (gold FIND A BATTLE, slab PRACTICE VS AI / OPEN GUILD / FULL STANDINGS, quiet locked RANKED chip), two-tone leaderboard rows with a gold №1 edge, a blue rim on your own head, tighter zones sized to their content, and the drifting glyph background every other tab has.

Online hub: the Battle zone is now a proper mode select — a big QUICKPLAY tile with RANKED and PRACTICE VS AI stacked beside it — and every zone (trade offers, guild, leaderboards) fills its space with bigger, readable text instead of tiny labels and empty gaps.
